deities: Lord Hanuman (reclining ~6-foot idol, head facing north)

history.dynasty: None documented (folk/legendary origins; temple developed by mahants)
history.period: Legendary antiquity; temple/monastery establishment attributed to Sri Balgiriji ~1119 AD (verify)
history.summary: Shri Bade Hanuman Ji Mandir near Triveni Sangam is famous for its rare ~6-foot reclining Hanuman idol, head to the north and feet to the south, in an underground sanctum. Legend holds Hanuman rested here after burning Lanka (one account: while ferrying the Sanjeevani herb for Lakshman), and that the idol was unearthed by the saint Baghambari Baba after a dream when he came for the Kumbh Mela centuries ago; the math is managed by Baghambari Gaddi (Niranjani Akhara). One travel source attributes a temple/monastery establishment to Sri Balgiriji around 1119 AD and a possible 14th-15th century idol origin (verify). It is called the Kotwal (guardian) of Prayagraj, and devotees believe a Maha Kumbh bath is incomplete without Hanuman's darshan here. CSV TOWN FLAG: CSV town 'Allahabad' - the city was officially renamed Prayagraj in 2018; documented as Prayagraj.

name: Bade Hanuman Ji Mandir
town_description: Prayagraj (formerly Allahabad) is the sacred city at the Triveni Sangam - the confluence of the Ganga, Yamuna and mythical Saraswati - and the site of the Kumbh and Magh Melas. It is a major Hindu pilgrimage centre as well as a historic city with the Mughal-era Allahabad Fort, Anand Bhavan and Prayagraj University.

travel.road: Near Triveni Sangam in the Dariyabad area; the new Akshayavat corridor entrance is ~500 m away; auto-rickshaw/taxi from Sangam or the station

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Tuesdays; Magh Mela/Kumbh Mela (very crowded)
